data.description: A benign primary cardiac tumor composed of dense collagen and fibroblasts, most often arising intramurally in the ventricular wall (especially the left ventricle).
symptoms_in_common: Single, well-circumscribed intramural mass in the left ventricle
Homogeneous, intense late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI (fibrous tissue)
Echogenic, relatively avascular-appearing mass on echocardiography
Gross specimen firm, tan-white, rubbery nodule ~3–4 cm
Histology showing dense collagen with bland spindle cells and entrapped small vessels; Masson trichrome highlighting abundant collagen; no atypia/mitoses
symptoms_not_in_common: Infiltrative margins with destruction of adjacent myocardium

data.description: An intraventricular blood clot often forming along akinetic/dyskinetic endocardial surfaces after infarction or with severe cardiomyopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Subendocardial location along the left ventricular cavity
symptoms_not_in_common: Homogeneous intense late gadolinium enhancement (thrombus typically shows no or only peripheral enhancement)
Firm tan-white tumor-like gross specimen rather than friable clot
Histology lacking collagenous stroma and fibroblasts (thrombus would show fibrin/organization)
Well-circumscribed intramural growth (thrombus is intracavitary and mural-adherent, not intramural)

data.description: The most common benign cardiac tumor, usually arising from the left atrial septum as a pedunculated, gelatinous mass that can be mobile and embolize.
symptoms_not_in_common: Ventricular intramural location (myxomas are typically left atrial and intracavitary, attached to the fossa ovalis)
Homogeneous dense collagen on histology rather than myxoid stroma with stellate cells and hemorrhage
Firm, fibrous gross appearance instead of gelatinous, friable mass

data.description: A benign hamartomatous tumor of cardiac muscle, most common in infants and associated with tuberous sclerosis; often multiple intramyocardial nodules.
symptoms_not_in_common: Homogeneous intense late gadolinium enhancement from dense fibrous tissue (rhabdomyomas typically show less LGE and different signal)
Single lesion rather than multiple nodules
Firm collagenous gross specimen rather than softer muscle tumor

data.description: A rare malignant cardiac tumor that is infiltrative, often rapidly enlarging, with heterogeneous enhancement, necrosis, and histologic atypia.
symptoms_in_common: Left ventricular mass with enhancement on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of necrosis or hemorrhage on imaging and gross exam
Histology lacking cellular atypia, high mitotic activity, or malignant vascular channels
Firm collagen-rich mass rather than heterogeneous malignant tissue
